This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-04-2019 at about 1:00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760, from Nayandahalli Bus Stop side to R.R. Arch side, on Mysore road, near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru.

At that time, the Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came at high speed from R.R. Arch side on the other side of the said road, which is bifurcated by a stone Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/
2 median and suddenly took a right turn where there is a provision for the same to go to Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, without giving any signal to the vehicles either coming on his back side or coming in front of the said Tata 407 Tempo and without observing the vehicles plying on the other side of the said road and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner, which was also being ridden by its rider at high speed, in rash and negligent manner.

In order to avoid the accident, the rider of said scooter took the same to the extreme left side of the road, due to which the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body and the said Honda Dio Scooter was also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Fortis Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment and thereafter he was shifted to SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie and was earning sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle and driver of the Tata 407 Tempo for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tata 407 Tempo and the respondent No.3 is the owner and respondent No.4 is the rider of the Honda Dio Scooter.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
Whereas, the respondent No.4 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.4 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him.
Further, it has denied the manner of accident as narrated in the petition.
It has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further it is contended that, the driver of its Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 was driving the vehicle slowly, carefully and cautiously, observing all traffic rules and regulations came from R.R. Arch towards Nayandahalli and when he reached near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, for the puspose of filling the diesel to the vehicle, showing the indicator, slowly taking right turn towards Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, at that time the rider of scooter along with a pillion rider, without wearing helmet and without holding valid driving licence, riding a Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.

No.KA-04-ED-4760, doing wheeling on one wheel, came from Nayandahalli towards R.R. Arch in Mysore road at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules and regulations, so as to endangering human life and property, all of a sudden came and dashed against the left side door and safety guard of the battery of the respondent No.1 vehicle.
The driver of its vehicle has lodged a complaint against the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.

to the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police
. The police have registered the case against the rider of said scooter and seized the said two-wheeler and issued notice under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, to its RC owner i.e. respondent No.3.

For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.1.

It has contended that, there is a negligence on the part of the petitioner himself to proceed as a pillion rider on the Honda Dio Scooter bearing No.KA-04-ED-4760 by not taking proper care and precaution, since the said petitioner was talking with the rider of the said scooter and shaking by his act, which is a clear negligence on the part of the petitioner.

The rider of the Honda Dio Scooter was also negligent in riding the said scooter by not following traffic rules and regulations, as he was wheeling i.e. lifting the front wheel of the said scooter and was riding the said scooter on the back wheel, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the tempo bearing No.KA-05-AF-8462.

Hence, the police have charge-sheeted the rider by name Mohammed Afreed S/o Taj Mohammed, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. and Section 189, 3(1) R/w 181, 146 R/w 196, 5 R/w 180 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is a self evidentiary to point out that the rider of the scooter was not holding driving licence to ride the said scooter and was riding the same in rash and negligent manner, at the time of accident.

Further it is contended that, there is no insurance policy to the Honda Dio Scooter, both petitioner/pillion rider and rider of the said Honda Dio Scooter were not wearing helmets at the time of accident.
There is negligence on the part of petitioner himself and also negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Dio Scooter.

On the other hand, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AF-8462, as he was driving the said vehicle slowly, carefully and following all traffic rules and regulations.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the insurer of the Honda Dio Scooter has not been made as party to the proceedings.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-04-2019 at about 1.00 p.m., near Indian Oil petrol bunk, Nayandahalli, Bengaluru city, due to composite rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata 407 tempo bearing registration No.KA-05-AF- 8462 and riding of the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA-04-ED- 4760 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04- ED-4760 and Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF- 8462 in the said accident and the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the rider of offending vehicle/Respondent No.4, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above facts and circumstances of the accident averred by the petitioner and has taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding of the rider on Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04- ED-4760, who was wheeling the said scooter on one wheel and while so doing he lost control over the said vehicle and dashed against the left side door and safety guard of the battery of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg.

. Further it is contended that, there is absolutely no negligence on the part of the driver of said Tata 407 Tempo and hence, the police have filed the charge-sheet against the rider of said Honda Dio Scooter and not against the driver of Tata 407 Tempo.

Whereas, the respondent No.3, who is the owner of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 04-ED-4760 as on the date of accident, has also denied the above facts and circumstances of the accident averred by the petitioner and has taken specific defence that, it is clear from the entire police records that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider/subsequent purchaser of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-ED-4760 i.e. respondent No.4.

But, the driver of said Tata 407 Tempo in order to escape from the liability has lodged a false complaint against the respondent No.4 and in collusion with the police has falsely impleaded her in the present proceedings.

Though, the respondent No.3 has taken specific contention that, the accident has taken place due to composite negligence of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-ED-4760, has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

Except, the self serving statements of respondent No.3/R.W.4, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.3 to establish that, the accident has taken place due to composite negligence of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 and the investigation officer has foisted false charge-sheet against the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED- 4760/respondent No.4 alone.

Further, though the said rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 has been made party to this proceedings as respondent No.4 and notice of present petition has been duly served on him, he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

sentences.text: As rightly contended by the respondent No.1 & 2, the entire police investigation records available in record clearly goes to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the respondent No.4.

Except the self serving statement of P.W.1,
there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AF-8462 was driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and the said accident has taken place due to composite negligence of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760.
Even there is no evidence on record which goes to show that, there was any contributory negligence on the part of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 in the cause of accident.

15. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on Mysore road, near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Nayandahalli, Bengaluru, due to dashing of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 to the left side door and safety guard of the battery of Tata 407 tempo, which came from R. R. Arch side road and took right turn towards Indian Oil Petrol Bunk.

The learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, the Ex.P.4 sketch clearly speaks that, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 tried his level best to avoid the accident, but as the Tata 407 tempo came with high speed from R.R. Arch side and suddenly took a right turn to go to Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, without giving any signal and without observing the vehicles plying on the said road, he could not avoid the said accident and as such the said accident has taken place due to composite rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462 and the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-ED-4760.
Hence, the owner and insurer of both the vehicles are liable to compensate the petitioner, for the injuries caused to him in the said accident.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on the following judgments:

On meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch, it clearly reveals that,
the said accident has not taken place soon after the Tata 407 tempo took right turn from R. R. Arch side road, but the same has occurred after it took right turn from R.R. Arch side road and had almost crossed the half portion of the road and was just 10 feet away from the entrance of Indian Oil Petrol Bunk and the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- ED-4760, which was proceeding towards the right side of the road, just beside the center median of the road, came towards the left side of the said road and dashed against the Tata 407 tempo.

In such circumstances, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner does not holds good and the ratio laid down in the above cited judgments are not applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

Further it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, there is no damage caused to the Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-8462, whereas the front portion of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 is extensively damaged in the said accident.

In such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, the question of composite rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of Tata 407 Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-05- AF-8462 does not arise at all.
17. Further, as per the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata 407 Tempo, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata 407 Tempo or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.R.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-ED-4760.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the rider of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident , rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

18. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary and Ex.P.8 emergency consultation sheet, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous Arbaaz Khan vs Nandi Glass And Plywoods on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62286034/

sentences.text: The petitioner has suffered (1) nose deformed, active bleeding from nose, (2) lacerated wound 1 cm x 1cm over lower lip, (3) right ear canal hemotympanum and (4) pan facial fracure.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

19. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.

sentences.text: But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident in question, he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered physical disability and he is not in a position to perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his learning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 9 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11 and 13.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.2,29,369/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,29,369/- under the head of medical expenses.

iii) Pain and sufferings: In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. (1) nose deformed, active bleeding from nose was present, (2) lacerated wound 1 cm x 1cm present over lower lip, (3) right ear canal shows hemotympanum and pan facial fracture.
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 24-04-2019 to 30-04- 2019, in SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/-
is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 = Rs.7,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 7 = Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Gangondanahalli, Bengaluru South,
Nayandahalli, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred on near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Nayandahalli,
Bengaluru, and he has taken treatment at SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before the accident he was working as coolie and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month.

sentences.text: The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2019.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.

viii) Loss of amenities: It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 20 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 7 days as in-patient in SSNMC Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, it might have took 2 months for complete curing of the injuries suffered by him.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,32,969/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
24. Liability:

The oral and documentary evidence available on record clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.3 was the owner of offending Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED- 4760.

The respondent No.3 has taken specific contention that, as on the date of accident she was not the owner of the offending Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04- ED-4760, as she had already sold the said vehicle to one Rajesh M. S/o Mani, on 27-08-2015, for sale consideration of Rs.3,000/-.
But, the respondent No.3 has failed to prove the said contention.
She has not produced any document to show that, as on the date of accident she was not the owner of offending vehicle and alleged Rajesh M. S/o Mani was the registered owner of said vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ED-4760 the accident in question has occurred and he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was not insured.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.3 being the owner of said offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused to the petitioner by the said vehicle.

Accordingly, holding that the respondent No.3 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount Rs.3,32,969/- to the petitioner, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,32,969/- (Rupees three lakh thirty two thousand nine hundred and sixty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.3 is directed to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner within one month from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.1, 2 & 4 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
